Fireball: how the code works

A walk through the game's C code: what touches the hardware, how one frame runs, and what the numbers are. Line numbers refer to main.c unless another file is named. The README covers how to play and how to build.

Layout

 main.c / main.h            gba.c / gba.h              Game Boy Advance
 ┌────────────────────┐     ┌────────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────────────────┐
 │ state machine      │────►│ waitForVBlank()    │────►│ scanline counter  0x4000006 │
 │ player, fireballs  │     │ fillScreenDMA()    │────►│ DMA registers     0x40000B0 │
 │ collisions, timer  │     │ drawImageDMA() ... │────►│ video memory      0x6000000 │
 │ reads BUTTONS      │─────┼────────────────────┼────►│ buttons           0x4000130 │
 └────────────────────┘     └────────────────────┘     └─────────────────────────────┘
          ▲
          │ #include "images/*.c"  (nin10kit arrays: screens and sprites)

main.c includes the image .c files directly, so they compile as part of main.o. The Makefile links gba.o, font.o, main.o and the course's example image images/garbage.o.

Hardware the game touches

All addresses are in gba.h and gba.c.

What Address Used for
REG_DISPCNT 0x4000000 set to MODE3 | BG2_ENABLE once at start-up (line 32)
SCANLINECOUNTER 0x4000006 frame timing in waitForVBlank()
DMA 0x40000B0 the four DMA channels; the game uses channel 3 (DMA[3], at 0x40000D4) for every screen clear and image draw
BUTTONS 0x4000130 button state; a pressed button reads as 0, so KEY_DOWN inverts it
videoBuffer 0x6000000 the 240 × 160 Mode 3 bitmap, one 16-bit value per pixel

Colours are 15-bit: COLOR(r, g, b) packs 5 bits each as r | g<<5 | b<<10 (gba.h line 25).

The state machine

enum gba_state {
    START,
    GAMEPLAY,
    STARTBG,
    WON,
    GAMEOVER,
};
From Event To Where
START A, B or R held STARTBG lines 61–80
STARTBG always, after one frame GAMEPLAY line 101
GAMEPLAY the player overlaps a lit fireball GAMEOVER line 128
GAMEPLAY frame count reaches the goal WON line 141
GAMEPLAY, WON, GAMEOVER Select held START lines 167, 175, 182

START, WON and GAMEOVER redraw their full-screen image every frame. STARTBG resets the player to (20, 80), gives every fireball a random position and speed, marks them all unlit, and sets the frame counter to 0.

One frame of gameplay

The GAMEPLAY case (lines 104–169) runs these steps in order:

  1. waitForVBlank() waits for the screen to enter VBlank and adds one to vBlankCounter.
  2. fillScreenDMA(BLACK) clears the screen.
  3. For each fireball: draw it if lit, move it, and if it is lit and overlaps the player, set GAMEOVER.
  4. Draw the player sprite (20 × 20).
  5. Draw the timer at row 150: seconds survived (vBlankCounter / 60), a slash, and the goal in seconds.
  6. If vBlankCounter has reached the goal, set WON.
  7. Light fireball number vBlankCounter / 360.
  8. Read the D-pad and move the player one pixel, kept inside x 0–220 and y 0–140.
  9. If Select is held, set START.

The state changes in steps 3, 6 and 9 take effect on the next pass of the loop, so the last one set in a frame wins.

Frame timing

void waitForVBlank(void) {
    while(SCANLINECOUNTER > 160);
    while(SCANLINECOUNTER < 160);
    vBlankCounter++;
}

The first loop waits while the display is past line 160, in the rest of a VBlank already under way. The second loop waits until the display reaches line 160, the first line of VBlank. The game counts these frames as its clock and shows 60 of them as one second. It uses polling, not interrupts.

Movement, bouncing and collisions

Each fireball moves by its own xd and yd, in pixels per frame, and reverses an axis when the next step would leave the screen (y between 0 and 150, x between 0 and 230, both exclusive):

if ((fireballs[i].y + fireballs[i].yd < 150) && (fireballs[i].y + fireballs[i].yd > 0)) {
    fireballs[i].y += fireballs[i].yd;
} else {
    fireballs[i].yd= -fireballs[i].yd;
    fireballs[i].y += fireballs[i].yd;
}

Collisions are an overlap test of two axis-aligned boxes, only for lit fireballs:

if ((fireballs[i].state == 1) &&((p.x < fireballs[i].x + fireballs[i].w) && (p.x + p.w > fireballs[i].x) && (p.y < fireballs[i].y + fireballs[i].h) && (p.h + p.y > fireballs[i].y))) {
    state = GAMEOVER;
}

Modes and the lighting schedule

Mode numFireballs ndeltas (speeds drawn from {1, 2, 3, 4}) vblankthreshold (goal) Fireballs lit by the goal
Easy (A) 2 1, so speed 1 600 (10 s) 2: at 0 and 6 s
Medium (B) 5 2, so speed 1 or 2 1,500 (25 s) 5: at 0, 6, 12, 18, 24 s
Hard (R) 8 4, so speed 1 to 4 2,400 (40 s) 7: at 0, 6, … 36 s

Mode settings are at lines 62–78. A fireball's x and y speeds are drawn separately and both start positive: every fireball sets off down and to the right, unless it starts close enough to an edge to bounce at once.

Drawing with DMA

Images are copied to video memory one row at a time with DMA channel 3, source and destination both incrementing:

void drawImageDMA(int row, int col, int width, int height, const u16 *image) {
    for (int r = 0; r < height; r++) {
        DMA[3].src = &image[OFFSET(r, 0, width)];
        DMA[3].dst = &videoBuffer[OFFSET(row + r, col, 240)];
        DMA[3].cnt = width | DMA_ON | DMA_SOURCE_INCREMENT | DMA_DESTINATION_INCREMENT;
    }
}

fillScreenDMA uses the same loop with a fixed source (one colour value) for each of the 160 rows. Text is the exception: drawString and drawChar set pixels one at a time from the 6 × 8 font in font.c.

Image and font data

Array Source Size in bytes
start, gameover, won 240 × 160 PNGs 76,800 each, 230,400 together
sprite player, 40 × 40 PNG resized to 20 × 20 800
fireball 20 × 20 PNG resized to 10 × 10 200
fontdata_6x8 font.c 12,288

Sizes are the *_SIZE defines in images/*.h and the array length in font.c. The images were converted with nin10kit (--mode=3); each images/*.c header records the command. The repo records no ROM size, frame-rate or tearing measurement.

Quirks, left as built

  • On Hard the eighth fireball never lights: it would light at 2,520 frames (42 s), after the 2,400-frame goal.
  • Positions and speeds come from the C library's rand(), which the game never seeds, so the first game after power-on always starts the same way. randint() in gba.c is unused.
  • previousButtons is stored but unused (line 190), so buttons are read as held, not as newly pressed.
  • A fireball is drawn before it moves, so the collision test uses a position 1 to 4 pixels (per axis) away from where it is drawn.
  • undrawImageDMA() in gba.c is an empty stub.
